# N05. X9 wiring: K6 called from Megatron-Core's distributed optimizer, with the next forward's first parameter all-gather started inside the optimizer step

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Switch: `AK_X9_EARLY_AG=1` (config L20; the rest of the wiring is armed by K6's switches) · In the submitted runs: **on** · Class: **as K6** (E0-restricted: K6's norm pass only; the AdamW step E0) · Rule basis: Graph Execution (TR-8.3); with K6, Hyperparameters, optimizer paragraph (TR-9.1c) and Numerical formats (TR-5.2b)

**L4 v3.** This item is L4 v2's, byte for byte, in L4 v3's image: the same two patches and the same installed files. Where this write-up names L4 v2's image or test runs, that evidence was collected on L4 v2's package (`firmus_gb300_ngpu8_llama8b_l4_nvfp4_v2`, withdrawn from this submission; see [Index](../KERNELS.md)). This package's own ten runs print the same early all-gather line, all `True` (Evidence). In L4 v3, N11's no-overlap mode waits at their dispatch for the gathers the forward runs beside compute; bucket group 8, the embedding's, is the one this early all-gather gathers and waits for inside the optimizer step ([N11](N11_fp4g_patch.md)).

## In brief

NVIDIA's recipe runs Megatron-Core's distributed optimizer step with Transformer Engine's (TE's) `FusedAdam` and
Megatron's gradient-norm code; the next forward then gathers the bf16 parameters, the embedding's bucket group first.
N5 is the pair of Megatron-Core patches that route that step through K6 (X9) and, with `AK_X9_EARLY_AG`, start the
embedding's group's all-gather inside the optimizer step, between two phases of K6's step. N5 adds no arithmetic: the
norm's all-reduce, root and clip coefficient stay Megatron's, the arithmetic is K6's (class as K6), and the early
all-gather gathers the same bytes, sooner. Every scored run compares the early-gathered buffer with a synchronous
re-gather: 0 of 1,221,623,808 elements differ. N12 relies on this early all-gather, and no code ties the two together.

## What it replaces (Replaces)

- **NVIDIA's code** (both chains in Equivalence). Megatron-Core's `DistributedOptimizer` keeps fp32 master weights
  sharded across the data-parallel ranks (each rank owns one contiguous range, a "shard", of each parameter) and the
  bf16 parameters in Megatron's parameter buffer (`param_data`, one bf16 buffer per bucket, which the all-gathers
  fill). Its step uses fp32 gradient copies, TE's `multi_tensor_l2norm`, `multi_tensor_scale_tensor` and `FusedAdam`,
  and a master-to-bf16 copy. With `overlap_param_gather=True` the parameter all-gathers (one coalesced all-gather per
  bucket group) run in the next forward as a chain, from the last group built to the first; the first is the group
  holding the embedding weight ("the embedding's bucket group"; bucket group 8 of 9 in the submitted runs, `result_1.txt` L916, L918),
  which the forward dispatches and waits for at once.
- **What N5 changes.** No fp32 gradient copies: each master is bound to a bf16 view of its gradient shard. The local
  norm: K6's norm pass over those views. The scale pass: the clip coefficient is stashed and applied inside K6's fused
  step. `FusedAdam` and the bf16 copy: K6's fused step, in two phases when the early all-gather is on. K9's separate
  weight-amax pass: K9's buffer (held by N6, the nvfp4p patch) is passed to the step's epilogue. The forward's first
  gather: started inside the optimizer step, between the two phases. The equations of the step, the norm and the
  epilogue are K6's ([K06](K06_x9step3_fused_adamw.md), Equivalence and Optimizer).

## Why the result is the same (Equivalence)

NVIDIA's step, per rank, in stock Megatron-Core:

```
prepare_grads          g32 = fp32(g_bf16) for every gradient shard
clip_grad_norm         n_loc = multi_tensor_l2norm(g32);  total = sqrt(all_reduce_sum(n_loc²))
                       c = min(1, max_norm / (total + 1e-6));  g32 = g32 · c
step_with_ready_grads  FusedAdam.step();  p_bf16 = bf16(p) into the parameter buffer
next forward           all-gather the embedding's bucket group (dispatch, wait), then each other group in turn
```

With N5 (stock code where not named):

```
prepare_grads          bind each master to its bf16 gradient view (no copy)
clip_grad_norm         n_loc = K6 norm pass(g_bf16);  total and c as stock;  c stashed
step_with_ready_grads  FusedAdam.step()   (no bf16-master parameter has a .grad, so it skips them)
                       K6 fused step, phase 1: this rank's shards of the embedding's bucket group
                       dispatch that group's all-gather (asynchronous)
                       K6 fused step, phase 2: every other shard (with the epilogue)
                       stream wait for the gather; mark the group gathered
next forward           that group: the mark found, only the next group's gather dispatched; then as stock
```

Stock references (Megatron-LM `f6c33bde`): `optimizer/distrib_optimizer.py` `_copy_model_grads_to_main_grads`
L2767-2811 (the fp32 copy at L2803), `_copy_main_params_to_model_params` from L2813, `step_with_ready_grads`
L3202-3233; `optimizer/clip_grads.py` `get_grad_norm_fp32` L59-144, `clip_grad_by_total_norm_fp32` L147-196 (the
coefficient at L183, the clamp at L186, the scale at L190-192); `optimizer/optimizer.py` `prepare_grads` L772-805,
`step_with_ready_grads` L808-844 (`optimizer.step()` at L817, the copy at L839);
`distributed/param_and_grad_buffer.py` `start_param_sync` L427-582, `finish_param_sync` L584-619 (dispatch if not
dispatched, L601-604; wait, L606-608; start the next group, L610-619), and the gradient sync marking every group's
gather as not dispatched before the optimizer step (L850); `distributed/distributed_data_parallel.py`, the gather
chain L386-397 and the forward pre-hook L534-557.

Why each piece gives the same bytes:

- **The arithmetic is K6's**: byte-identical to TE's chain outside K6's stated norm domain
  ([K06](K06_x9step3_fused_adamw.md), Equivalence). N5 hands K6 the operands TE's chain uses: the bf16 gradient bits
  the stock fp32 copy is made from (that copy is exact), the masters, m and v, and the parameter group's
  hyperparameters, read at every step.
- **The norm's reduction stays Megatron's**: the square, the all-reduce, the root and the clip coefficient. Only the
  local norm is K6's. The gradient list uses the stock filters (not shared, not a tensor-parallel duplicate) with the
  bf16 view in place of the fp32 `.grad` (patch `mcore/0001` L143-162).
- **The two phases**: K6 treats each shard on its own, with the same host scalars, so splitting the shard list in two
  changes no byte (tested: Evidence, the shard-grouping test and the closed loops).
- **The early all-gather** is Megatron's own `start_param_sync` for that bucket group (a coalesced all-gather of each
  rank's shard into the group's parameter buffer), issued sooner.
  - It is dispatched after every phase-1 call of every parameter group, so this rank's shards of the group are written
    (patch `mcore/0001` L266-271). Phase 2 skips every shard of that group (L234-235).
  - At the end of the step the stream waits for the gather (no host sync), the handle is cleared and the group is
    marked gathered (L325-328, called at L375-377). The forward's first wait for the group finds the mark, clears it
    and only starts the next group's gather (L59-66). A forced synchronous parameter sync, as around evaluation, clears
    the mark (L69-72), so those gathers run as stock.
  - Bucket group 8 is one of the two groups that K15 leaves to Megatron's bf16 gather (`result_1.txt` L916: "mixed
    groups {0: … output_layer.weight, 8: … word_embeddings.weight}"), so the early gather moves bf16 bytes through
    Megatron's code. Its first result is compared with a synchronous re-gather (Enablement).
  - A review of the stream order found that the dispatch follows phase 1 on the default stream, the wait comes before
    the graph replay, the replay runs on the stream that waited, and no compute-stream reader of bucket group 8 runs
    between the dispatch and the wait (record R9).
- **The patch's own note** says nothing in the arithmetic changes, only the order of independent work. That is true of
  the arithmetic; the early all-gather is not independent of N12 (The coupling with N12, below).

**Class: as K6.** N5 computes nothing of its own: it routes the step through K6 and moves one all-gather. Its class is
K6's, **E0-restricted** through K6's norm pass only; the AdamW step is E0. The norm could differ from TE's only if every
non-zero gradient element feeding some partial sum of the norm pass has |g| < 2^-63; it has never been observed (the
in-training shadows and the closed loops found the norm byte-identical, Evidence). The domain, and why training stays
outside it: [K06](K06_x9step3_fused_adamw.md), Equivalence. The early all-gather moves bytes and computes nothing.

### The coupling with N12

- N12 (smallk2) replaces the recipe's embedding forward and reads `word_embeddings.weight` directly (`firmus/ak/pkg/ak_l8b_smallk2_patch.py` L155-156).
  It calls neither the embedding module, whose forward pre-hook is where DDP waits for the embedding's bucket group's
  all-gather, nor Megatron's `ensure_params_ready` (provided for readers ahead of the owning module's pre-hook).
- With N5's early all-gather on, as submitted, that group is gathered and waited for inside the optimizer step, before
  the next forward, so N12 reads current weights. **N12's equivalence relies on N5's early all-gather.**
- With it off, the group's gather is first started by layer 0's pre-hook, after N12's read, so the other ranks'
  embedding rows are one step stale.
  Measured (DP 4, mock data; record R3): training then leaves stock at step 3 (11.498331069946289 against
  11.498795509338379), deterministically, at 50 and at 200 steps, identically with the rest of X9 on or off. With
  N12's embedding path off as well (`AK_SMALLK2_EMB=0`), it equals stock (8 steps; record R4).
- No code ties the two together: neither patch checks the other's switch; N12's first-call check runs on the warm-up's
  fully gathered weights, so it cannot see a missing gather; no run-start gate row covers the early all-gather
  ([N12](N12_smallk2.md)). N5's own equivalence does not depend on N12.

**State kept between calls:** no data values, only addresses, lists and flags. Patch `mcore/0001`: the gradient views
(L127-136); per parameter group and phase a K6 instance with its lists, plus the early-gathered group and phase counts
(L193-252); the weight-amax slots (L283-301); a bound-gradients flag (set L141, cleared L103); the clip coefficient,
stashed every step (L184-187; patch `mcore/0002` L75-76), asserted (L262), cleared after every fused step (L106-108);
an in-flight flag (L271, cleared L329), the mark on bucket group 8 (set L328; cleared by the forward's first wait, L61,
or a forced sync, L70-71) and a once-only check flag (L330-332). Patch 0002: its norm instance and a printed-once flag
(L22-23, L34-37). K6's cached tables: K06 (read from patch `mcore/0001` L53-75, L97-109, L119-357 and patch
`mcore/0002` L8-45, L68-79).

## Numerics (Numerics)

As K6 ([K06](K06_x9step3_fused_adamw.md), Numerics). N5 adds no floating-point operation: the norm's square,
all-reduce and root are Megatron's code, and the overriding `clip_grad_norm` computes the coefficient with the same two
fp32 tensor operations as Megatron's `clip_grad_by_total_norm_fp32` (patch `mcore/0001` L184-186). The early all-gather copies bf16 bit patterns.

## Optimizer and gradient clipping (Optimizer, Gradient clipping)

- **Optimizer.** The equations, the hyperparameters and the A/B against TE's and apex's `FusedAdam` are K6's
  ([K06](K06_x9step3_fused_adamw.md), Optimizer). N5 reads lr, betas, eps, weight decay, the step count and the
  bias-correction flag from the parameter group at every step (patch `mcore/0001` L274-280),
  so the warm-up's changed values and the scheduler's learning rate reach K6 as they reach TE's `FusedAdam`.
- **Gradient clipping.** The coefficient's two code paths and why it is unchanged: [K06](K06_x9step3_fused_adamw.md),
  Gradient clipping. N5 hands it over: stashed by the `clip_grad_norm` override or by Megatron's
  `clip_grad_by_total_norm_fp32`, which then skips the scale kernel when no fp32 gradient is left to scale (patch `mcore/0001` L184-187; patch `mcore/0002` L75-78),
  and applied inside the fused step. Clipping is not deferred and not computed from partial data.

## Inputs it accepts (Shape specialisation)

### Gate

- **The wiring arms** as K6 arms (patch `mcore/0001` L119-123): `AK_X9_E0=1`, the module loaded, not a stub optimizer,
  not Megatron-FSDP, no precision-aware optimizer, no reuse of the gradient buffer for an MXFP8 parameter gather.
  Otherwise the stock chain runs ([K06](K06_x9step3_fused_adamw.md), Gate).
- **The early all-gather arms** when `AK_X9_E0=1` and `AK_X9_EARLY_AG=1` (L47) and the layout is the plain one
  (L303-318): `overlap_param_gather` on, one model chunk, bucket groups present and no expert-parallel bucket groups,
  and the last bucket group built heads the gather chain (no group names it as its next). Otherwise rank 0 prints
  `early all-gather NOT armed: the bucket layout is not the plain one` and the step runs in one phase (L217-225), with
  every gather in the forward as stock.
- **Raises** if: the gradient buffer is not bf16 (L134); a parameter is quantized (L207); a separate gradient-norm
  group exists, which would need a second clip coefficient (L212-214); the optimizer state is missing or not fp32
  (L237-238); no clip coefficient was stashed before the fused step (L262); the weight-amax buffer belongs to another
  optimizer (L292-293); fp32 model parameters carry gradients (L170-171), so no fp32 parameter can be copied into the
  buffer after the early gather's dispatch; the early-gathered buffer differs from the synchronous re-gather (L354-356).
- **Falls back to stock, by design:** no gradients bound since the last fused step: the stock master-to-bf16 copy
  (L97-102); any non-bf16 gradient in the norm's list: TE's `multi_tensor_l2norm` (patch `mcore/0002` L55-61); N6's
  weight-amax table not built yet: the step without the epilogue (patch `mcore/0001` L288-291), in the submitted runs
  the warm-up's first optimizer step; a layout that is not the plain one: no early all-gather, one phase.
- In the submitted runs the early all-gather armed (Evidence); `overlap_param_gather: True` is in every log's
  configuration (`result_1.txt` L132, L402).

### Assumptions not checked in code

- **The early all-gather is on whenever N12 is armed** (The coupling with N12). What keeps it true: the leaf sets
  `AK_X9_EARLY_AG=1` (config L20), and its line is a proof line, in
  all ten logs (`result_1.txt` L918). If it failed: a silent wrong result; the other
  ranks' embedding rows would be one step stale, and training leaves stock at step 3.
- **Nothing reads or writes the embedding's bucket group's parameter buffer between the dispatch and the wait**, except
  the gather. What keeps it true: phase 2's calls, the epilogue included, touch only phase 2's shards, by construction;
  the stream wait comes before anything queued on that stream after the step; the stream-order review found no such
  reader (Equivalence). If it failed: a silent wrong result for the reader (a partly gathered buffer); the once-only
  check compares after the wait.
- **Megatron's other gather-scheduling options are off.** The arming test checks `overlap_param_gather` but not
  `align_param_gather` (gathers dispatched from the pipeline schedules) or `overlap_param_gather_with_optimizer_step`.
  What keeps it true: both are False in all ten logs (`align_param_gather=False`, `result_1.txt` L402;
  `overlap_param_gather_with_optimizer_step=False`, L405). If it failed: with `overlap_param_gather_with_optimizer_step`,
  Megatron dispatches every group's gather again after the step (stock `optimizer.py` L1747-1752), and the forward's
  first wait for the embedding's group would return without waiting for that second gather (patch `mcore/0001` L59-66).
  Not analysed further; no check declines it.
- **As K6** (N5's patch makes these calls; [K06](K06_x9step3_fused_adamw.md), "Assumptions not checked in code"):
  AdamW with `capturable` off; TE's `step()` has advanced the step counter before the fused step; the cached gradient
  views, lists and buffer views stay valid; the stock chain's fp32 copies are 16-byte aligned; no partial sum of the
  norm is a non-zero fp32 subnormal. Each would give a silent wrong result if it failed (`capturable`: not analysed).

### Benchmark detection

N5 reads no data, no benchmark identity and no step position. It picks the first-gathered bucket group from Megatron's
bucket layout and reads the hyperparameters live (Benchmark detection, TR-2.3).

## How it is switched on and checked at run time (Enablement)

- **Switch:** `AK_X9_EARLY_AG`, read when `distrib_optimizer.py` is imported (patch `mcore/0001` L47), default off, and
  effective only with `AK_X9_E0=1`. The leaf sets it with K6's three switches on config L20:
  `AK_X9_E0=1 AK_X9_FOLD=1 AK_X9_EARLY_AG=1 AK_X9_WAMAX=1`.
- **The rest of the wiring** is armed by K6's switches: `AK_X9_E0` (patch `mcore/0001` L27; the bound gradients, the
  norm and clip hand-off, the fused step), `AK_X9_FOLD` (patch `mcore/0002` L21; the norm pass) and `AK_X9_WAMAX`
  (patch `mcore/0001` L52; the epilogue); the kernel directory `AK_X9_KERNEL_DIR` defaults to `/opt/firmus/ak/x9`
  (patch `mcore/0001` L30; patch `mcore/0002` L25), as K6 ([K06](K06_x9step3_fused_adamw.md), Enablement). Their
  ARMED lines (patch `mcore/0002` L36-44; patch `mcore/0001` L253-257) and the epilogue's slot count (L297-300) are
  K6's; K06 quotes them.
- **First-call check of the early all-gather**, N5's only per-run verdict: once per run, at the first optimizer step
  with it armed, the warm-up's first, before `run_start`. Every rank re-gathers bucket group 8 synchronously from the
  same shards and compares every bf16 bit pattern with the early-gathered buffer (L333-356).
  - Each rank raises on its own difference; the count is not all-reduced, so a rank whose buffer differed would raise
    alone and the other ranks could then block. A raise in the warm-up ends the job before `run_start`.
  - At that step NVIDIA's warm-up has set lr and weight decay to 0 (`callback_warmup.py` L237-245; Megatron-Bridge
    steps the scheduler only after the optimizer step, `training/train.py` L974 and L1002, read on development image
    0929's copy, the same Megatron-Bridge), so the parameters do not change in it. The check shows that the gathered
    buffer is complete and equal to a synchronous re-gather; the order of the gather after phase 1's writes rests on
    the stream order (Equivalence) and the model-level comparisons (Evidence).
  - Only rank 0's line reaches the log, and it prints no sha; the two installed files are bound by the banner, which
    re-hashes the stack record (it lists both) and prints MATCH.
  - No run-start gate row covers this check; the gate's verdict is per rank
    ([Enablement and fail-loud behaviour](../KERNELS.md#enablement-and-fail-loud-behaviour)).

## Approval (Approval)

- **Graph Execution (TR-8.3).** "Frameworks are free to optimize the non-weight parts of the computation graph
  provided that the changes are mathematically equivalent." The early all-gather issues the same gather of the same
  bytes earlier, after the values it gathers are written; the routing of the step through K6 is K6's case.
- **With K6:** Hyperparameters, optimizer paragraph (TR-9.1c), and Numerical formats (TR-5.2b) for gradient clipping;
  the arguments and the class are K6's ([K06](K06_x9step3_fused_adamw.md), Approval). N5 changes no hyperparameter
  and no clipping.
- **The coupling.** N5's equivalence does not depend on N12; N12's depends on N5's early all-gather (The coupling with
  N12; [N12](N12_smallk2.md)).
- No exception is requested; no Equivalence exceptions (TR-9.5) exception is needed.

## Evidence (Evidence)

**Result on the submitted image:** PASS (E0-restricted, as K6): in each of this package's ten scored runs the
early-gathered bucket group equalled a synchronous re-gather (0 of 1,221,623,808 elements), and in two identity loops
on this image armed L4 v3, N5 included, equalled stock's reference in all 1,152 losses and the evaluation (DP 4, a
device synchronize at every step end); the byte-level tests of the step ran on L4 v2's image (below).

### Tests on the submitted image

- **Import and banner** ([Tests on the built image](../KERNELS.md#5-tests-on-the-built-image)): the clean image imports
  `firmus_ak` and prints banner MATCH; the stack record it re-hashes lists both installed files with the same sha256
  as L4 v2's image (`fb84d2a5`, `023bd6ee`; record R11). No kit grades N5's two files; the 24 re-targeted development
  kits, K6's among them, passed 48 / 48.
- **Arithmetic identity** (record R12): two loops of armed L4 v3 with the submitted leaf, one tray each (DP 4), a
  device synchronize at every step end, seed 4243, 1,152 steps, evaluation at step 768. In both, the 1,152 losses and
  the evaluation (5.51950740814209) equal stock's reference exactly, and all 56 proof lines, N5's among them, printed
  `True`. A 2 × 4 smoke run of the submitted configuration, 800 steps, also printed every proof line `True`.

### Checks in every scored run

- In each of this package's ten logs (`result_0.txt` … `result_9.txt`), once, at L918, with no "NOT armed" or
  "self-check FAILED" line in any (`result_1.txt` L918; the next line, L919, is "Finished warmup step 0"):

  ```
  0: [auto_kernel x9step] early all-gather ARMED: bucket group 8 of 9 (23 params, 1221623808 elements) gathered inside the optimizer step between phase 1 (6 shards) and phase 2 (38 shards); the gathered buffer against a synchronous re-gather: 0 of 1221623808 elements differ: True
  ```

  Phase 1 holds rank 0's 6 shards in bucket group 8 and phase 2 its other 38, of the 44 in K6's ARMED lines
  (L914-915). The line is one of the 56 proof lines Firmus's post-run check required in every scored log of this
  package (record R11).
- The banner prints `stack_sha256=024dd9bc…`, then `MATCH` (`result_1.txt` L69-70; once in each log). The run-start
  gate line (L946) lists 19 armed parts, none of them the early all-gather, and ends `True`; `run_start` follows at L950.

### Tests on L4 v2's image

L4 v2's submitted image; its files differ from L4 v3's only in N11's module, the run-start gate, the leaf's one added
switch, four comments or docstrings, and the three rebuilt extensions (K10, K11, K12).

- **Installed bytes** (record R1): both installed files MATCH (`fb84d2a541dc433b`, `023bd6eeea4f3db6`), among the 35
  of 35 package files checked in the image. No kit grades `distrib_optimizer.py` or `clip_grads.py` (record R10).

  own chain re-run on clones of each rank's shard. `distrib_optimizer.py` was a test-only copy, the installed file

  of every rank: 0 mismatches in the fused step, the epilogue and the norm pass; eager mode, 18 steps: 0 mismatches.

- **Step-boundary bytes** (record R8): the early all-gather runs at the boundary between an optimizer step and the next
  forward pass; in the run-to-run loops of armed L4, the bytes of the items at that boundary, N5's among them, were
  identical up to every departure ([Run-to-run reproducibility](../KERNELS.md#run-to-run-reproducibility)).
